rawFindings.title: Incorrect comment about className check in writeObject
rawFindings.explanation: The comment on line 332 states the check is for 'java.utils.HashMap', which is incorrect; it should be 'java.util.HashMap' matching the DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map value. This inconsistency can cause confusion.
rawFindings.suggestion: Update the comment on line 332 from 'java.utils.HashMap' to 'java.util.HashMap' to accurately reflect the class name being checked.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect condition for treating class name as empty in writeObject function
rawFindings.explanation: In the method writeObject, the condition to treat the class name as empty incorrectly uses only 'obj.$class === javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map', removing the handling for 'iMap' which was removed mistakenly. This change breaks support for the interface map class name in the encoding process, which previously correctly treated 'java.util.Map' as empty class name.
rawFindings.suggestion: Restore the condition to include both 'javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map' and 'javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.iMap' in the comparison to treat their class names as empty, for example: className = obj.$class === javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map || obj.$class === javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.iMap ? '' : obj.$class;

rawFindings.title: Incorrect handling of java.util.Map when determining className in writeObject
rawFindings.explanation: In proto.writeObject, the condition to clear className for map types removed handling of javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.iMap ('java.util.Map'). This breaks correct serialization of objects with $class 'java.util.Map' as they are no longer treated as untyped map, which is inconsistent with previous behavior and likely incorrect.
rawFindings.suggestion:
Restore the check for both javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map and javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.iMap when setting className to empty string, i.e., use:
className = obj.$class === javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.map || obj.$class === javaObject.DEFAULT_CLASSNAME.iMap ? '' : obj.$class;
